object_description: staggered building structure of three parts with a cantilever over the tight slope-side access
geometry_property: corner projecting over the sports hall
design_condition: the staggered structure follows the neighbouring development along the street and reacts to the sloping terrain so it fits naturally into the hillside landscape

positive: The staggered structure is based on the development structure along the street
Staggering lets the body react appropriately to the sloping terrain
It fits naturally into the hillside landscape
The diverse accessibility integrates the complex well into the surrounding neighbourhood
The project promises a simple and sensible arrangement of uses inside
Outdoor spaces with different uses are created and connected by ramps and steps
The choice of plant material addresses and develops the vegetation of the nearby green belt
The outdoor space designed close to nature promises good robustness for use
Both school parts have an atrium with a spiral staircase leading upwards
The spatial connection of the two parts seems attractive at first glance
Two classrooms with two group rooms and a common cloakroom form a unit on the upper floors
Inside, the facade bands create a playful and child-friendly element
The rooms appear bright and attractive
The disposition with three volumes and two lit inner courtyards promises great potential
negative: The access area on the slope is very tight
The cantilevered structure proposed to compensate seems architecturally unfortunate
It undermines the division into three parts and weakens the basic design idea
The main entrance is difficult to find under the overhang and is much too small
The two atriums adjoining escape corridors must be glazed for fire safety
This significantly weakens the quality of the interior concept
The classroom unit does not entirely meet user needs as the lounges are centrally placed below
The facade with meandering bands appears very heavy despite its materiality
Whether external insulation suits a school building of this size is questioned for sustainability
Economic efficiency and sustainability requirements were only just exceeded in some cases
The authors are unable to exploit the potential of the disposition
The corner projecting over the sports hall cannot be realised in the dimensions shown
